items.title: "Visibly Reverses 10 Years": 5 Skincare Label Words Decoded (SkinCeuticals, L'Oréal, Lancôme)
items.description:
SkinCeuticals says its $185 serum "visibly reverses 10 years." L'Oréal once said its creams boosted your genes, until the FTC stepped in. Here are 5 words on skincare labels and what each one actually has to prove.

CHAPTERS
0:00 Five words on the box
0:25 1 · Clinically proven (FTC v. L'Oréal)
1:16 2 · Visibly (cosmetic vs drug)
2:03 3 · Dermatologist tested
2:31 4 · Up to (SkinCeuticals TNXA-Shot: 30% vs 22%)
3:16 5 · The 8× multiplier
4:12 The Folio Card
4:43 Note for deeper skin
4:58 The Folio Bench

THE FOLIO CARD: LABEL WORDS DECODED
• Clinically proven: who ran it, how many people, how long, this exact product?
• Visibly: appearance only, usually judged by eye
• Dermatologist tested: usually a safety check, not a results test
• Up to: the best case. Look for the average.
• 8×: ask, than what?

FREE NEWSLETTER: one Folio Card a week → https://theformulafolio.com

THE FOLIO BENCH: own a luxury product with a big claim on the box? Film a 10-second swipe on your forearm in daylight and send it to hello@theformulafolio.com. We may feature it (no faces needed).

SOURCES
• FTC, "FTC to L'Oréal: Scientific claims need proof that's more than just skin deep," June 2014; FTC final order, L'Oréal USA (Génifique, Youth Code)
• FDA, "Wrinkle Treatments and Other Anti-aging Products"; FDA warning letter to Lancôme USA, Sept 7, 2012
• FTC, consumer perception study of "up to" claims, June 2012
• SkinCeuticals TNXA-Shot launch release, PR Newswire, Nov 17, 2026 (study fine print)
• Lin FH et al., J Invest Dermatol 2005;125:826–832 (pig skin, ~8-fold photoprotection)
• Murray JC et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 2008;59:418–425 (human skin)
